chief_data.selection_justification: Candidate 1 (τ=0.6 min, Q=0.5 mL/min) is selected as the first screen. Both candidates share identical hardware (reactor_cuc_cart_030, 0.3 mL Cu/C CatCart, 20 bar BPR, 150 °C), identical safety scores (1.000), and identical PVS (0.672). Candidate 1 scores marginally higher on combined (0.823 vs 0.812), chemistry (0.820 vs 0.750), and kinetics (0.720 vs 0.680) domains. The gap is within 5%, triggering tiebreak: (a) safety is equal; (b) the researcher objective is a practical first experiment — Candidate 1's higher Q (0.5 mL/min) gives a shorter nominal space time (0.6 min vs 0.75 min), providing a more aggressive first data point against the 3-min batch benchmark and a 5× residence-time reduction vs the 4× of Candidate 2; (c) Q=0.5 mL/min sits comfortably within the pump envelope (0.1–3.0 mL/min) and the design envelope (0.35–0.65 mL/min), making it the more defensible protocol-based starting exposure. Candidate 2 is retained as the first step-down in a τ-sweep. Neither candidate has experimentally validated kinetics, holdup, or pressure drop in this packed bed; the conversion figure (X≈1.00) is an unvalidated screening proxy based on batch-inferred first-order kinetics with a 10× intensification factor and must not be treated as a demonstrated result.
chief_data.selection_rationale: Candidate 1 wins on combined score (0.823 vs 0.812) and on both chemistry and kinetics sub-scores, with both candidates sharing perfect fluidics, safety, and geometry scores. The score gap is within 5%, so the tiebreak was applied: safety is equal (1.000 each); the researcher objective — a practical first flow experiment — favours the higher-throughput, shorter-τ point (0.6 min, 0.5 mL/min) as it provides the most aggressive initial comparison against the 3-min microwave batch, achieving a nominal 5× residence-time reduction. The design envelope confirms Q=0.5 mL/min is well-centred (±30% window: 0.35–0.65 mL/min) and the 20 bar BPR comfortably exceeds the hard minimum of 11.81 bar required to suppress acetone boiling at 150 °C. The most critical remaining uncertainty is actual liquid holdup and contact time in the Cu/C packed bed: the nominal τ=0.6 min is a geometric (empty-bed) space time and the true catalytic contact time depends on bed voidage, particle size, and wetting efficiency — none of which are measured. The second major uncertainty is whether the heterogeneous Cu/C catalyst activity in flow matches the batch loading (10 mol% Cu); catalyst leaching, deactivation, and bed channelling are uncharacterised. The first bench experiment should therefore verify steady-state conversion by collecting three consecutive 1-min fractions after 5τ (≥3 min) of equilibration, analysing by TLC or HPLC, before any optimisation is attempted.
resolved_tradeoffs: id=1 vs id=2: Both use identical hardware (reactor_cuc_cart_030, 0.3 mL, 4.0 mm ID, 20 bar BPR, 150 °C). Score gap is 1.3% (within 5% tiebreak threshold). Tiebreak resolved by researcher objective: Q=0.5 mL/min (id=1) gives τ=0.6 min (5× batch reduction) vs Q=0.4 mL/min (id=2) giving τ=0.75 min (4× batch reduction). id=1 is the more aggressive and informative first data point.
Design envelope id=1: τ [0.42–0.78 min], Q [0.35–0.65 mL/min], T [135–165 °C], BPR [18–26 bar, hard min 11.81 bar]. All within hardware limits.
Design envelope id=2: τ [0.52–0.98 min], Q [0.28–0.52 mL/min], T [135–165 °C], BPR [18–26 bar, hard min 11.81 bar]. All within hardware limits.

Both envelopes are fully contained within pump (0.1–3.0 mL/min, 40 bar) and reactor (40 bar, 200 °C) hard limits. id=2 envelope is retained as the first step-down in a τ-sweep if id=1 shows incomplete conversion.

r_mix flags (111.1 for id=1, 88.9 for id=2): These are empty-tube diffusion proxies and are not applicable to a packed bed. Packed-bed radial mixing is governed by particle-scale convection and is expected to be superior to the empty-tube estimate. Flag is advisory only and does not disqualify either candidate.

Da_mass=2456 for both candidates: This is an empty-tube proxy and is not applicable to the packed bed. Actual mass-transfer resistance depends on particle size, voidage, and superficial velocity — unmeasured. Conversion estimate is unvalidated.
BPR hard minimum: At 150 °C, acetone vapour pressure ≈ 11.8 bar. The 20 bar BPR provides a 8.2 bar margin above the suppression threshold. This is the only available BPR in inventory and is adequate.

Packed-bed particle-scale convection dominates radial mixing. Empty-tube r_mix is not a valid disqualifier for this reactor type. Concern is advisory.

Model validity explicitly states hydraulics and mixing models are not applicable to packed bed. Da_mass is an empty-tube proxy. Actual mass transfer in Cu/C packed bed is unmeasured and cannot be assessed from this proxy. Concern is advisory; measurement is required.

overridden_concerns.override_reason: Conversion is explicitly flagged as an unvalidated screening proxy. It is not used as a design gate. The screen is selected to measure actual conversion, not to confirm a predicted value.

remaining_uncertainties: Actual liquid holdup and catalytic contact time in the Cu/C packed bed are unknown. Nominal τ=0.6 min is a geometric empty-bed space time; true contact time depends on bed voidage, particle size, and wetting — none measured. This is the primary uncertainty.

Cu/C catalyst activity, loading uniformity, leaching rate, and deactivation profile in continuous flow at 150 °C are uncharacterised. Batch loading (10 mol% Cu) may not translate directly to a packed-bed cartridge.

Pressure drop across the packed bed is unresolved (empty-tube proxy gives ΔP≈0, which is not a packed-bed estimate). Actual ΔP must be measured at steady state to confirm operation within the 40 bar pump limit.

Benzyl azide is a primary organic azide: energetic hazard classification and thermal stability at 150 °C under flow conditions must be confirmed before scale-up. The blast shield (safety_cuaac_shield) is mandatory for all runs.
chief_data.experiment_recommendation: SETUP: Install Cu/C CatCart (reactor_cuc_cart_030, 0.3 mL, 4.0 mm ID) in the X-Cube cartridge holder. Set BPR to 20 bar. Set heater to 150 °C. PRIME: Pump pure acetone at Q=0.5 mL/min until system reaches thermal steady state and pressure stabilises at 20 bar (allow ≥5 min). REACTION: Prepare premixed feed solution: benzyl azide (0.25 M) + phenylacetylene (0.275 M, 1.1 equiv) in acetone. Switch pump feed to reaction mixture at Q=0.5 mL/min. EQUILIBRATION: Allow ≥5τ (≥3 min, use 5 min conservatively) before collecting product. COLLECTION: Collect three consecutive 1-min fractions into amber vials (collector_amber_100) behind the blast shield. ANALYSIS: Analyse each fraction by TLC and/or HPLC to determine conversion and triazole yield. SHUTDOWN: Flush with pure acetone at Q=0.5 mL/min for ≥5 min before cooling. SAFETY: All operations behind azide-service blast shield and secondary containment (safety_cuaac_shield). Confirm benzyl azide thermal stability data before proceeding. NOTE: Reactor volume is fixed at 0.3 mL (inventory); τ=0.6 min is the nominal empty-bed space time at Q=0.5 mL/min. True catalytic contact time will differ from this nominal value due to bed voidage; treat τ as a flow parameter, not a validated kinetic residence time. No gas phase is present; inlet/STP gas flow and pressure-corrected in-channel gas flow are both zero and not applicable to this all-liquid system.

final_consensus.X_estimated_note: Unvalidated screening proxy based on batch-inferred first-order kinetics with 10× intensification factor. Must be measured experimentally.
final_consensus.productivity_note: Theoretical maximum assuming X=1.00 and MW(triazole)≈249 g/mol; unvalidated until conversion is measured.
final_consensus.residence_time_basis: nominal empty-bed liquid space time (V_R_geometric / Q_liquid); not measured catalytic contact time
final_consensus.gas_phase: none — all-liquid system; inlet/STP gas flow = 0 sccm; pressure-corrected in-channel gas flow = 0 mL/min

pump_flowrates.role: single premixed substrate feed (benzyl azide + phenylacetylene in acetone)
pump_flowrates.derivation: Feed rate is taken directly from the inventory-realized candidate solution, which jointly solves stoichiometry and hardware bounds. Verification: ṅ_limiting (benzyl azide) = Q_A × C_feed = 0.500 mL/min × 0.25 mmol/mL = 0.125 mmol/min. Phenylacetylene delivery = 0.500 mL/min × 0.275 mmol/mL = 0.1375 mmol/min = 1.1 equiv relative to benzyl azide. No batch-productivity heuristic applied; rate is set by the declared hardware solution.
pump_flowrates.molar_equiv_basis: benzyl azide is reference (1.0 equiv); phenylacetylene is 1.1 equiv co-dissolved in same feed stream
pump_flowrates.note: All-liquid feed. No gas stream. Inlet/STP gas flow and pressure-corrected in-channel gas flow are both zero and not applicable.
